title: Dune II: The Battle for Arrakis
prompt: Build Dune II: The Battle for Arrakis as a multi-file web real-time strategy game — the game that set the template, so the template has to be there in full. The economy is spice: harvesters drive out to spice fields, fill up, drive back to a refinery and unload into credits, and credits are the only thing that pays for construction, which means a harvester lost is an economy stalled. Sandworms roam the open sand and swallow units that linger. Building works through a construction yard: you buy a structure from a sidebar list, then place it on the map, and it must be placed adjacent to existing buildings on prepared concrete, or it takes damage from the sand. Structures unlock further structures and units in a per-house tech progression, and power plants must keep up with demand or everything runs degraded. Give the three houses genuinely different rosters — Atreides, Ordos and Harkonnen, each with a unique unit and its own feel. Units need real orders (move, attack, guard, harvest, repair), turrets need firing arcs, and the enemy AI must build its own base, expand its economy and mount attack waves rather than spawning units from nowhere. Wrap it in the campaign: a map of Arrakis where the player picks the next territory to attack, with a mentat briefing before each mission and fog of war over unexplored ground.
